title: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals, Heavy Metals & Control

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016:
1. They replaced the Municipal Solid Wastes (Management and Handling) Rules, 2000.
2. They require waste generators to segregate waste at source into biodegradable, non-biodegradable and domestic hazardous streams.
3. They apply only within the limits of municipalities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2016 Rules widened the net beyond municipal limits to urban agglomerations, census towns, notified industrial townships, airports, railway stations and similar areas, so statement 3 is wrong. Segregation at source is the heart of the Rules.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals
questions.h: Three bins: wet, dry, domestic hazardous.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The thickness of plastic carry bags was increased from 50 microns to 75 microns in 2021 and to 120 microns from December 2022.
2. The ban on identified single-use plastic items under the Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules came into force on 1 January 2022.
3. The 2022 guidelines on Extended Producer Responsibility for plastic packaging classify plastic packaging into four categories, including rigid, flexible and multi-layered plastic.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The ban on identified single-use plastic items took effect on 1 July 2022, not January. The EPR guidelines use four categories: rigid, flexible, multi-layered plastic packaging, and compostable plastic.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q: In the context of waste management, 'Extended Producer Responsibility' means that
o: producers, importers and brand owners are made responsible for the environmentally sound management of their products at the end of life
consumers are fined for littering used products
only municipal bodies must set up recycling plants
manufacturers are exempted from waste rules if they use recycled raw materials
questions.e: EPR shifts the burden of collecting, recycling or disposing of used products back to those who put them on the market. This gives producers an incentive to design for recyclability.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about e-waste regulation in India:
1. Extended Producer Responsibility for e-waste was first introduced through the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2016.
2. The 2016 Rules introduced the concept of Producer Responsibility Organisation and a Deposit Refund Scheme.
3. The E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 provide for a system of EPR certificates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: EPR for e-waste goes back to the 2011 Rules (in force from 2012). The 2016 Rules strengthened it with PROs, deposit refund and dismantler-recycler roles, and the 2022 Rules added certificate-based EPR.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Match List-I (Colour of bag/container under the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016) with List-II (Waste):
List-I: A. Yellow  B. Red  C. White (translucent)  D. Blue
List-II: 1. Anatomical waste, soiled waste and expired medicines  2. Contaminated recyclable plastics such as tubing, catheters and IV sets  3. Needles and other sharps in puncture-proof containers  4. Glassware and metallic body implants
questions.e: Yellow takes waste to be incinerated or deep-buried, red takes plastics to be autoclaved and recycled, white takes sharps, and blue takes glass and implants.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals
questions.h: Yellow = body; Red = rubber/plastic; White = needles; Blue = glass.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about landfills:
1. Leachate from landfills can contaminate groundwater.
2. Landfill gas consists largely of methane and carbon dioxide.
3. Sanitary landfills need no liner because the underlying soil always prevents the movement of leachate.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Decomposing organic waste produces methane (a potent greenhouse gas) and a toxic leachate. Sanitary landfills therefore have liners, leachate collection and gas collection systems.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Statement-I: Open burning of mixed waste containing PVC plastics releases dioxins and furans.
Statement-II: Dioxins and furans are formed when chlorine-containing materials are burnt at relatively low temperatures.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: PVC supplies chlorine, and incomplete combustion at modest temperatures lets that chlorine recombine with carbon into dioxins and furans. High-temperature, controlled incineration destroys them far more completely.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q: The Solid Waste Management Rules, Plastic Waste Management Rules, E-Waste Management Rules and Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules in India have all been framed under the
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
questions.e: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is the umbrella law that lets the Central Government make rules on hazardous substances and waste.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bhopal gas disaster of December 1984 was caused by the leak of methyl isocyanate from a pesticide plant.
2. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was enacted after the disaster.
3. The Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 requires victims to prove negligence by the owner before relief is paid.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Public Liability Insurance Act works on a no-fault basis: owners handling hazardous substances must insure themselves, and victims get immediate relief without proving negligence.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q: Which one of the following rules provides for the setting up of Crisis Groups at the Central, State, District and Local levels to deal with chemical accidents?
o: Chemical Accidents (Emergency Planning, Preparedness and Response) Rules, 1996
Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989
Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016
questions.e: The 1996 Rules build a four-tier crisis-management structure for major chemical accidents, while the 1989 Rules deal with safe manufacture, storage, import and on-site and off-site emergency plans.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q: The Insecticides Act, 1968, which regulates the import, manufacture, sale, transport and use of pesticides in India, is administered primarily by the
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
questions.e: Pesticides are regulated through the Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee under the agriculture ministry, even though their environmental effects fall under the environment ministry's laws.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Match List-I (Metal) with List-II (Associated health effect):
List-I: A. Mercury  B. Cadmium  C. Lead  D. Arsenic
List-II: 1. Itai-itai disease  2. Minamata disease  3. Neurological damage and reduced intelligence in children  4. Blackfoot disease and skin lesions
questions.e: Itai-itai ('ouch-ouch') came from cadmium in Japan's Jinzu river, causing bone and kidney damage; Minamata disease came from mercury in fish. Chronic arsenic exposure causes skin lesions and cancers.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q: Inorganic mercury discharged into water bodies becomes far more hazardous when bacteria in the sediment convert it to
questions.e: Methylmercury is fat-soluble and readily absorbed, so it bioaccumulates and biomagnifies up the food chain to large predatory fish. It attacks the nervous system, as in Minamata disease.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q: The site of a closed mercury thermometer factory, which became a well-known case of mercury contamination in India, is at
questions.e: The Kodaikanal factory in Tamil Nadu was closed in 2001 after protests over mercury waste. Bhopal is linked with the methyl isocyanate leak, Eloor with industrial pollution of the Periyar and Kanpur with tannery chromium.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about lead:
1. Lead is a cumulative toxicant that affects neurological development in children.
2. Lead is an essential micronutrient required by humans in trace amounts.
3. Lead does not accumulate in the body because the body excretes it quickly.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Lead has no known biological role. It accumulates in bones and soft tissue and especially harms the developing brain, which is why leaded petrol and lead-based paints were phased out.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about thermal treatment of waste:
1. Pyrolysis is the thermal decomposition of waste in the absence of oxygen.
2. Gasification converts waste by partial oxidation into a combustible gas mixture called syngas.
3. Plasma arc technology operates at temperatures below 200 degrees Celsius.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Plasma arc treatment uses extremely high temperatures, typically thousands of degrees Celsius, which is why it can destroy hazardous waste and dioxins; the 'below 200' claim describes ordinary low-temperature processes.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about phytoremediation:
1. In phytoextraction, hyperaccumulator plants take up heavy metals from the soil into their harvestable parts.
2. The metal-rich plant biomass, after harvest, can be disposed of as ordinary compost without any precaution.
3. It is an in situ method of cleaning contaminated soil or water.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The harvested biomass concentrates the very metals that were removed from the soil, so it must be treated as hazardous waste or processed for metal recovery. Using it as ordinary compost would return the metals to the environment.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about endosulfan:
1. It was aerially sprayed on cashew plantations in Kasaragod district of Kerala, with serious health effects reported.
2. The Stockholm Convention listed it for global elimination in Annex A in 2011.
3. It was one of the original twelve persistent organic pollutants listed in 2001.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Endosulfan was added to the Convention in 2011, a decade after the original 'dirty dozen'. Its health toll in Kasaragod made it a prominent domestic and international case.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about microplastics:
1. They are plastic particles smaller than 5 mm.
2. Secondary microplastics arise from the fragmentation of larger plastic items.
3. Microbeads deliberately added to some personal-care products are examples of secondary microplastics.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Microbeads are manufactured at tiny size, so they are primary microplastics. Secondary ones come from the weathering and breakdown of bottles, bags, fishing nets and tyres.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of plastic types and their resin identification codes:
1. Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) : 1
2. High-density polyethylene (HDPE) : 2
3. Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) : 3
4. Polypropylene (PP) : 4
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Polypropylene is code 5; code 4 is low-density polyethylene (LDPE). The sequence runs 1 PET, 2 HDPE, 3 PVC, 4 LDPE, 5 PP, 6 PS, 7 others.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals
questions.h: Pet, Hard-pe, PVC, Light-pe, PP, PS.

questions.q: In 2019, India amended the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules to
o: permit the import of solid plastic waste for recycling in all industrial zones
allow import of used lead-acid batteries without any permission
ban all export of electronic waste
prohibit the import of solid plastic waste, including into Special Economic Zones and Export Oriented Units
questions.e: Concerned about dumping of plastic scrap from abroad, especially after China's import ban, India prohibited the import of solid plastic waste.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016:
1. They extended the Rules to vaccination camps, blood donation camps and similar health camps.
2. They required the phasing out of chlorinated plastic bags, gloves and blood bags within a stipulated period.
3. They apply only to hospitals having more than 50 beds.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rules apply to every person who generates, collects, receives, stores or handles bio-medical waste, with no bed-size limit. Chlorinated plastics were targeted because their burning releases dioxins.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q: As per the Regulation of Lead Contents in Household and Decorative Paints Rules, 2016, the permissible lead content in such paints is not to exceed (in parts per million)
questions.e: The 2016 Rules under the Environment (Protection) Act tightened the earlier limit of 600 ppm to 90 ppm, because lead in paint dust is a major source of childhood lead exposure.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Statement-I: The effluents of tanneries are a major source of chromium pollution in the Ganga at Kanpur.
Statement-II: Hexavalent chromium is carcinogenic.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Tanning uses chromium salts and the discharged chromium contaminates water and groundwater. The carcinogenicity of Cr(VI) explains why it is dangerous, but not why tanneries are a source of it.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about waste-to-energy and bio-energy initiatives:
1. The SATAT initiative promotes setting up of compressed biogas plants using agricultural residue, municipal solid waste and cattle dung.
2. GOBAR-Dhan is a scheme administered by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
3. SATAT was launched by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: SATAT (2018) aims to create a market for compressed biogas as a vehicle fuel with oil marketing companies buying from entrepreneurs. GOBAR-Dhan sits under the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation of the Jal Shakti Ministry, not agriculture.
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Match List-I (Convention) with List-II (Subject):
List-I: A. Basel Convention  B. Rotterdam Convention  C. Stockholm Convention  D. Minamata Convention
List-II: 1. Prior informed consent procedure for certain hazardous chemicals and pesticides in international trade  2. Control of transboundary movement of hazardous wastes and their disposal  3. Elimination or restriction of persistent organic pollutants  4. Protection of human health and environment from mercury
questions.e: Think of Basel as waste, Rotterdam as trade consent, Stockholm as long-lived toxins, and Minamata as mercury.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions
questions.h: B-R-S-M: Basel Bins, Rotterdam Receipts, Stockholm Slow-poisons, Minamata Mercury.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Basel Convention:
1. It regulates the transboundary movement of hazardous wastes and their disposal.
2. It was adopted in 1989 and entered into force in 1992.
3. The United States has ratified it and is a full Party.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The United States signed but has not ratified the Basel Convention, so it is not a Party. The Convention was a response to toxic-waste dumping in developing countries in the 1980s.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Stockholm Convention allows a limited, acceptable use of DDT for disease vector control.
Statement-II: DDT is listed in Annex B of the Convention, which covers restriction, rather than in Annex A, which covers elimination.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Annex B chemicals are restricted to defined acceptable purposes, and malaria control by indoor residual spraying is one of them. Annex A chemicals must be eliminated with only specific exemptions.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions
questions.h: A = Abolish; B = Bound; C = Cooked up by accident.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Annexes to the Stockholm Convention:
1. Annex A lists chemicals for elimination.
2. Annex B lists chemicals for restriction.
3. Annex C lists chemicals for reducing unintentional releases, such as dioxins and furans.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Annex C targets by-products formed unintentionally in combustion and industrial processes, such as dioxins and furans, with the aim of continuing minimisation.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic generally used to classify a substance as a persistent organic pollutant?
o: Rapid breakdown by sunlight within a few days
questions.e: A POP survives for years, builds up in fatty tissue, travels via air and water far from its source (reaching the Arctic) and is toxic. Quick photolysis would remove it from the environment.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Minamata Convention on Mercury:
1. It is named after the Japanese city where severe mercury poisoning from industrial discharge occurred.
2. It contains provisions on artisanal and small-scale gold mining.
3. It requires every existing mercury mine to be closed immediately upon the Convention's entry into force.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Convention bars new primary mercury mines and phases out existing ones over a period of years, rather than closing them overnight.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q: Under the Minamata Convention on Mercury, which one of the following mercury-containing items is subject to a phase-down rather than a phase-out?
questions.e: Thermometers, most batteries, certain lamps and mercury cosmetics are scheduled for phase-out; dental amalgam is on the phase-down list because no equally affordable substitute was available everywhere.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rotterdam Convention:
1. It was adopted in 1998.
2. It promotes shared responsibility and information exchange in the international trade of certain hazardous chemicals.
3. It imposes a global ban on the production of all chemicals listed in its annex.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Rotterdam does not ban production. It requires that an importing country give prior informed consent before listed chemicals are exported to it.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q:
Arrange the following conventions in the chronological order of their adoption:
P. Stockholm Convention
Q. Basel Convention
R. Minamata Convention
S. Rotterdam Convention
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Basel (1989) dealt with wastes, Rotterdam (1998) with trade in chemicals, Stockholm (2001) with POPs and Minamata (2013) with mercury.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bamako Convention : Bans import of hazardous wastes into African countries
2. Waigani Convention : Bans import of hazardous and radioactive wastes into the South Pacific island countries
3. Basel Ban Amendment : Prohibits export of hazardous wastes from developed (Annex VII) countries to other countries
4. Rotterdam Convention : Prior informed consent for trade in certain hazardous chemicals and pesticides
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: These regional treaties grew out of frustration that Basel only regulated, rather than banned, waste trade. The Basel Ban Amendment entered into force in 2019.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q: The Convention on Long-range Transboundary Air Pollution (1979), which addresses problems such as acid rain, was adopted under the auspices of the
o: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe
questions.e: Acid rain from sulphur emissions in one European country was damaging the forests and lakes of its neighbours, so UNECE negotiated this regional framework, the first legally binding multilateral treaty on transboundary air pollution.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 48A, a Directive Principle, directs the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.
2. Article 51A(g) makes it a fundamental duty of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment.
3. Both these provisions were inserted by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Both provisions came through the 42nd Amendment of 1976, in the aftermath of the 1972 Stockholm Conference. The 44th Amendment (1978) dealt with property and Emergency safeguards.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q:
Match List-I (Legal principle) with List-II (Case):
List-I: A. Absolute liability for hazardous industries  B. Polluter pays principle applied to sludge-producing chemical industries  C. Precautionary principle and sustainable development  D. Public trust doctrine
List-II: 1. Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India  2. M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum gas leak)  3. Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. Union of India  4. M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath
questions.e: After the Oleum gas leak, the Supreme Court went beyond the English rule in Rylands v Fletcher to hold hazardous industries absolutely liable. The Kamal Nath case treated natural resources such as rivers and forests as held by the State in trust for the public.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions
questions.h: Oleum = Absolute; Bichhri = Polluter pays; Vellore = Precaution; Kamal Nath = Trust.

questions.q: Which one of the following Acts is NOT among the laws listed in Schedule I of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, over which the Tribunal has jurisdiction?
questions.e: The Tribunal hears civil cases under seven laws: the Water Act, Water Cess Act, Forest (Conservation) Act, Air Act, Environment (Protection) Act, Public Liability Insurance Act and Biological Diversity Act. Wildlife and the Indian Forest Act are outside its jurisdiction.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions
questions.h: Seven laws; Wildlife is not one.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Tribunal:
1. It was established in 2010 under the National Green Tribunal Act and is a specialised body for environmental disputes.
2. Its principal bench is at New Delhi, with zonal benches at Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai.
3. Appeals against its orders lie to the concerned High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Appeals against NGT orders lie directly to the Supreme Court, within 90 days. The NGT is guided by principles of natural justice and is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure or the Indian Evidence Act.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about air pollution control devices:
1. An electrostatic precipitator removes particulate matter by charging the particles and collecting them on oppositely charged plates.
2. A wet scrubber can remove gaseous pollutants such as sulphur dioxide.
3. Cyclone separators are the most effective devices for removing the finest particles (PM2.5).
4. Catalytic converters use lead as the main catalyst.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Cyclones remove coarse particles by centrifugal force; fine particles need ESPs or bag filters. Catalytic converters use platinum, palladium and rhodium, and lead would poison them.
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q:
Statement-I: Vehicles fitted with catalytic converters must use unleaded petrol.
Statement-II: Lead in petrol coats the catalyst surface and deactivates it.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Lead compounds from leaded fuel stick to the platinum-group metals and block the reactions, a process called catalyst poisoning. This is one reason leaded petrol had to go.
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the categorisation of industries by the Central Pollution Control Board:
1. Industries are categorised as Red, Orange, Green and White based on a pollution index.
2. White category industries are considered practically non-polluting and do not require consent from the State Pollution Control Board.
3. Green category industries are exempted from the requirement of any consent from the State Pollution Control Board.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Green category units still need consent, though it is given in a simplified manner. Only the White (non-polluting) category is exempt from obtaining consent.
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006:
1. It was issued under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
2. Category A projects require environmental clearance from the Central Government on the recommendation of an Expert Appraisal Committee.
3. Category B projects are appraised at the State level by the State Environment Impact Assessment Authority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Larger or more sensitive projects (Category A) are cleared by the Ministry, smaller ones (Category B) by the SEIAA. All of this rests on the 1986 umbrella Act.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q: In bioremediation, the addition of nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus to stimulate the growth of indigenous pollutant-degrading microbes is called
questions.e: Biostimulation feeds the microbes already present; bioaugmentation adds specially selected microbes from outside. Biosorption is the binding of metals by biomass.
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q: Which one of the following conventions guarantees public access to environmental information, public participation in decision-making and access to justice in environmental matters?
questions.e: The Aarhus Convention (1998), under UNECE, establishes these three pillars of environmental democracy. The Espoo Convention covers EIA in a transboundary context.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q: In March 2022, the United Nations Environment Assembly adopted a resolution to
o: ban all single-use plastics worldwide by 2030
phase out all plastic production by 2040
establish a global fund for beach cleaning only
develop an international legally binding instrument on plastic pollution
questions.e: The resolution launched negotiations in an Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee on a treaty covering the full life cycle of plastics, including marine plastic pollution.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the twelve persistent organic pollutants originally listed in the Stockholm Convention in 2001?
questions.e: The original 'dirty dozen' were aldrin, chlordane, DDT, dieldrin, endrin, heptachlor, hexachlorobenzene, mirex, toxaphene, PCBs, dioxins and furans. Endosulfan came later, in 2011.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions
questions.h: Dirty dozen: 9 pesticides, PCBs, dioxins, furans, HCB.

questions.q:
Consider the following principles:
1. Sustainable development
2. Precautionary principle
3. Polluter pays principle
4. Public trust doctrine
How many of the above are mandated by Section 20 of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 to be applied by the Tribunal while passing orders?
questions.e: Section 20 names three principles: sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle. The public trust doctrine is a judicial creation and is not mentioned in the section.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Environmental Legislation and Conventions
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions

questions.q: In many BS-VI diesel vehicles, a urea-based solution is injected into the exhaust in a Selective Catalytic Reduction system to reduce emissions of
questions.e: Urea decomposes to ammonia, which reacts with NOx over a catalyst to produce nitrogen and water. Particulates are handled by a diesel particulate filter.
questions.u: Pollution Control & Conventions
